newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn wants to stop war pensions to Nazi criminals.
newsitem.headline: Bonn wants to stop war pensions to Nazi criminals.

text.p: Germany said on Wednesday it was doing all it could to stop disability pensions being paid to convicted Nazi war criminals after a television documentary said thousands of these benefits were still being distributed.
"The German government and parliament are looking for ways to bar war criminals from receiving war-victim pensions," Chancellery Minister Friedrich Bohl said in a statement.

The government admitted in January that some Nazi war criminals were still receiving pensions after a television network said billions of marks (dollars) were being paid in disability pensions to them every year.
Bohl said there were still a few such cases but explained that this was due to a law passed after the war aimed at keeping pension and criminal issues separate.

Bohl stressed that some members of Adolf Hitler's Waffen SS elite forces were still entitled to disability pensions. "The Waffen SS was not just made up of voluntary members, but many were forcibly recruited Germans and foreigners," he said.

The NDR television documentary said about 50,000 war criminals and members of army units that took part in atrocities were receiving war disability pensions ranging from several hundred to several thousand marks each month.
